analysis: The only changed file is desktop-app/package-lock.json, a lockfile-only dependency refresh. Direct devDependencies move electron 44.5.1 to 44.9.1 (lock lines 24 and 3679) and vite 8.3.2 to 8.3.5 (lines 31 and 6677). Transitive bumps: rolldown and its @rolldown/binding-* packages 1.2.12 to 1.2.15, @oxc-project/types, postcss 8.5.28 to 8.5.32, nanoid 3.3.19 to 3.3.20, fast-uri 3.1.8 to 3.1.9, http-cache-semantics 4.2.0 to 4.3.0, undici 7.30.0 to 7.30.1 and the nested node-gyp undici 6.29.0 to 6.29.1. Every changed entry keeps a registry.npmjs.org resolved URL with an sha512 integrity hash. No dependency source changed to a git, file or non-registry URL, and no integrity field was removed. New metadata is limited to the "libc" fields on the linux rolldown bindings and an expanded @vitejs/devtools peer range. All of these sit in dev-only dependency trees ("dev": true), so they affect build and test tooling, not the provider runtime. The one runtime-adjacent component is the Electron version used by the desktop app build. This bump is a patch-level update within major 44 and no security regression is evident. The diff touches none of the threat-model assets (A-001 to A-018) or boundaries (TB-002, TB-003, TB-007, TB-009 to TB-012). I could not verify the upstream integrity hashes or the content of the new package versions from the supplied evidence. That is a supply-chain trust question, not an observed defect. The patch excerpt is truncated, but the base_text unit and the changed-range map are consistent with a lockfile-only change. Remaining integration questions: whether the CI install path uses npm ci with this lockfile, and whether the desktop app's Electron fuses and hardening configuration, not shown in this batch, are unaffected by the bump.
